title: Turn away from His remembrance, and a devil moves in.
subtitle: Blindness of the heart invites a bad companion
then: Ibn Kathir explains the word used comes from {trap}weakness of vision{/trap}, meaning here weakness of insight: willfully ignoring the remembrance of the Most Gracious. For that person {trap}a devil is assigned as a companion{/trap}.
now: You drop your morning adhkar for a few weeks. Not on purpose, just busy. Slowly the mornings fill with doomscrolling, irritation, a heavier mood. {trap}A heart does not stay empty.{/trap}
old: Skipping remembrance just leaves a blank space.
new: When I stop remembering Allah, something worse takes that space.
try: Bring back one small remembrance tomorrow morning: three times subhanallah before you get out of bed.

title: Pulled off the path, while sure they are guided.
subtitle: The danger of feeling right while going wrong

row.title: I feel fine, so I am fine

then: Ibn Kathir says for the one who willfully neglects guidance, {trap}a devil is sent to lead him astray and show him the path to Hell{/trap}. The frightening part is in the verse: {trap}they think they are guided{/trap}.
now: You feel completely sure in an argument, sure about a habit, sure about a grudge. Everyone around you is wrong. {idea}Feeling certain is not the same as being on the path.{/idea}
old: If I feel at peace with it, it must be right.
new: I can feel guided and still be drifting, so I check myself against revelation.
try: Ask one trusted, honest person: "Is there something I am doing that I cannot see is wrong?"

title: I wish you were as far from me as east from west.
subtitle: Regretting a companion on the Day
then: Ibn Kathir says when he comes before Allah on the Day of Resurrection, {trap}he will complain about the devil who was assigned to him{/trap}. He wishes the distance between them were as far as the east from the west.
now: The friend who always says "one more round," the online voice who makes everything cynical. You enjoy it now. {idea}Picture that friendship from the end, and ask if you will still want them close.{/idea}
old: My friends do not really affect who I become.
new: The companions I keep close now are the ones I will be judged alongside.
try: Spend time this week with one friend who reminds you of Allah.

title: Sharing the blame will not lighten it.
subtitle: Company in wrongdoing is no comfort later
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}your being together in the Fire will not help you in the slightest{/trap}, and both will share in the painful punishment. Having company in wrongdoing changes nothing.
now: At work, everyone pads their expense report a little. In the family, everyone gossips about the same aunt. It feels safer because it is shared. {idea}The verse says sharing it does not shrink your part.{/idea}
old: If everyone is doing it, it is not that bad.
new: A wrong shared with others is still fully mine.
try: Step out of one shared wrong this week, quietly, even if you are the only one.

title: You cannot make the deaf hear. That is not your job.
subtitle: Guidance belongs to Allah, the message to you
then: Ibn Kathir says this means {idea}that is not up to you{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ only had to convey the message, and {idea}Allah guides whom He wills{/idea}, being Wise and Just in that.
now: Your brother has stopped praying. You have tried talks, texts, videos, guilt. You lie awake feeling responsible. {idea}Your part is to be kind and clear. The heart is in Allah's hands.{/idea}
old: If someone I love does not change, it is my failure.
new: I deliver with love. Opening hearts is Allah's work, not mine.
try: Make dua for one person you have been trying to change, then let go of the pressure for today.

title: Even after you are gone, justice will come.
subtitle: The outcome does not depend on the Prophet's lifetime

row.title: it will happen
sub: whether I see it or not

then: The surah introduction notes the Makkan leaders were {trap}plotting day and night to end the Prophet's ﷺ life{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says the verse means {idea}We will inevitably punish them, even if you pass away{/idea}.
now: Someone wronged your family badly and seems to be doing fine. You worry you will die before anything is set right. {idea}The verse says the account stays open, whether or not you are there to see it close.{/idea}
old: If I do not see justice myself, it never happened.
new: Allah's justice does not wait on my lifetime.
try: Hand one old injustice over to Allah in a dua, and let yourself rest from carrying it.

title: Or We will show you. We are able to do both.
subtitle: Allah's full control over the outcome
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah is able to do both. As-Suddi's view, favored by Ibn Jarir, is that {reward}Allah would not take His Messenger ﷺ until He let him see his enemies brought low{/reward} and gave him power over them.
now: You are up against something huge: a company, a system, an illness. It feels unbeatable. {idea}Nothing is beyond His command.{/idea} How and when it turns is His to decide.
old: Some things are just too big to change.
new: Whatever I face is under the full command of Allah.
try: Write down the problem that feels too big. Under it write: "He has full command over this."

title: Hold tight to what was revealed. You are on the path.
subtitle: Steadiness under pressure
then: With plots all around him, the Prophet ﷺ is told to hold fast. Ibn Kathir says this means {idea}hold fast to the Quran which has been sent down to your heart{/idea}, for it is truth and leads to {reward}the straight path to the Gardens{/reward}.
now: Everyone around you is cutting corners and you start wondering if you are naive. The pressure is real. {idea}The verse does not say "relax." It says "hold tighter."{/idea}
old: When everyone pushes back, maybe I should loosen up.
new: Pressure is exactly when I hold on tighter to what Allah sent.
try: When you feel pressure to compromise today, recite one verse you know by heart before you decide.

title: An honor for you, and you will be asked about it.
subtitle: The Quran as both privilege and responsibility

picture.label: What it means to have it

row.title: a question
sub: what did you do with it

then: Ibn Abbas and others said this means {reward}an honor for you and your people{/reward}, revealed in their language, so they were most obliged to follow it. Ibn Kathir adds: {idea}you will be questioned about how you acted on it{/idea}.
now: Three copies of the Quran in your house, an app on your phone, a beautiful recitation in your car. It is easier to reach than ever. {idea}And one day the question: what did you do with it?{/idea}
old: Having the Quran in my life is the honor.
new: The honor comes with a question: how did I respond to it?
try: Choose one verse and act on it today in one concrete way.

title: Ask every messenger. They all said the same.
subtitle: One message across all prophets
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}all the messengers called their people to the same{/idea}: worship Allah alone, and leave idols and false gods. The Prophet ﷺ was bringing nothing new.
now: A friend tells you Islam is just one opinion among many. You realize you have never thought of it as the same message Ibrahim, Musa and Isa brought. {idea}One call, from the first messenger to the last.{/idea}
old: My faith is one tradition among many separate ones.
new: Every messenger called to the same thing: worship the Merciful alone.
try: Read the story of one other prophet this week and notice the same core message.
